$comment: Numbers for the docs' Scale pages. Regenerate with `bun tools/scale-bench-data.ts` from tools/results; do not edit by hand. Times are milliseconds, one per table size.

setup.dataset: orders (n rows: customerId (n%20000)+1, orgId (n%100)+1, status by n%5, paid n%2=0, createdAt evenly over 7 years to 2026-11-01, reference ORD-00000001) and customers (20,000 rows)
setup.client: one engine call at a time; paired requests 10+ rounds, other requests 10 calls (5 when the warm-up took over 1 s, 3 over 20 s); warm cache

profiles.out-of-the-box: The schema the benchmark starts with: primary keys, an index on orders (createdAt, id) and one on orders (customerId), trigram indexes on lower(orders.reference) and lower(customers.name). Exact counts; facets use the engine's default, facets.splitAbove 100,000.
profiles.tuned: a trigram index on lower(orders.status) (checkIndexes: fix.sql); orders.customerName copied from the customer, with the index the check then asks for (checkIndexes: advice (copy the name onto orders), then fix.sql for the new column); count: "capped" instead of "exact" (countCap 10,000) (engine option; checkIndexes reports exact-count-large-table from 1,000,000 rows); facets.splitAbove: 0, one statement per facet (engine option, from the facets guide; checkIndexes has no finding for it).
profiles.scoped: Tuned, with the resource scoped to one tenant of 100 (orgId 42): an index on (orgId, createdAt, id) for the scoped setting (applied by hand: checkIndexes describes the problem in words and gives no SQL). Capped counts.

setup.engineNote: Every timing is an engine call at commit 15da95f: pages and counts through queryIds, counts capped with count: "capped", facets through queryFacets, per-statement times from onQuery.

method: Every request runs through the engine, from Node over TCP, timed end to end. Counts that are capped use `count: "capped"`, facets go through `queryFacets`, and the engine's own per-statement times (`onQuery`) give the parts of a request. No number here is hand-written SQL.

A request that tuning changes is called against the out-of-the-box schema and the tuned one in turn, at least 10 rounds, in an order in which each follows the other equally often. Only those two schemas are resident in the database at a time. The benchmark calls a request faster or slower only when at least 80% of its rounds agree and the median ratio is at least 15% from 1; anything else reads "no change".
The same request against itself is timed as a control: a gain the control could have produced is reported as no change.

"Tuned" is what `engine.checkIndexes()` asked for plus the engine options that answer its findings; the table above lists every change and the finding behind it, and says which of them touches no timed request.
Numbers are warm-cache medians after an untimed identical call; a cold first request is slower.
